stem:
Ira sketches the stars at 8 p.m. in January. In February she looks again at 8 p.m. The night sky at that same clock time has changed. She is deciding whether Earth's rotation on its axis or Earth's revolution around the Sun explains the month-to-month change at the same clock time.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: The change from January's 8 p.m. sky to February's 8 p.m. sky comes mainly from Earth's revolution around the Sun.
The change from January's 8 p.m. sky to February's 8 p.m. sky comes mainly from Earth's rotation on its axis.
Earth's rotation and revolution are the same motion, so either word explains the February 8 p.m. change.
Night-sky changes at the same clock time from month to month do not involve Earth's motion at all.

teacher.key_rationale: Rotation is Earth turning on its axis; revolution is Earth moving around the Sun. The yearly change in the night sky at the same clock time comes from revolution.
